title: Frontend senior scenario production perf regression
topic: Frontend senior scenario production perf regression
question: Walk through how you'd diagnose and fix this, and how you'd prevent it from happening again.
idealAnswer:
Use real-user monitoring data (broken down by date, geography, device type, and connection speed) to narrow down when the regression started and whether it's uniform or concentrated in a specific segment, before looking at code at all

Bisect using deploy history against the regression's start date to narrow the range of candidate changes, rather than reading every PR from the last two weeks

Reproduce locally or in a controlled environment with profiling tools (Lighthouse, WebPageTest, Chrome performance panel) to pinpoint the actual bottleneck, whether it's a new render-blocking resource, a larger bundle, a slower API call the page waits on, or a layout shift pushing LCP later

Consider that LCP regressions are often caused by indirect changes, e.g. a new dependency added transitively, an A/B test injecting a blocking script, a CDN/cache config change, or a backend API getting slower, not just direct frontend code changes

Once found and fixed, add a regression safeguard, like a performance budget check in CI that would have caught this specific class of change before it shipped, not just fixing the one instance

Communicate root cause and impact to stakeholders with concrete before/after numbers, treating a Core Web Vitals regression with the same rigor as a functional production bug
